societies.name: Halo — Balaho under the Created

scope.period: The functioning alliance after Halo 5 and before the loss of Created control
scope.population: Living organic Unggoy residents; explicit alien-person proxy
exclusions: Every occupied human colony assigned Balaho’s benefits

societies.description:
Balaho is a concrete case where the Created’s promise becomes provision: advanced crewless ships and agricultural stations arrive, and food, shelter and medicine are supplied to the Unggoy. This supports a strong local material floor rather than inferring welfare from military dominance alone. The guarantee estimate still allows dependence on an external patron and the alliance’s durability. It does not assign identical treatment to human worlds that resist Cortana.

Control lies near autonomous AI authority because the Created direct the supporting infrastructure. Local acceptance does not make it equal resident ownership, though it avoids the same enforcement pattern imposed elsewhere. The modest nonworking estimate preserves the source’s active farmers, designers, crafters and revived factories. Having basic needs met can make useful work possible without making everyone idle. Unggoy are an explicitly named biological-person proxy, and the percentage is a broad editorial scenario rather than a census or a measure of agricultural automation alone.

guarantees.basis: Actual food, shelter and medicine support a strong but patron-dependent floor.

control.basis: The Created provide autonomous external support; local consent is not ownership.

nonworking.basis: Unggoy all-age scenario counts real farming, design, craft and care work despite supported basics.

societies.name: Transformers One — Sentinel’s Iacon

scope.continuity: 2024 animated film, separate from Aligned continuity
scope.period: The established regime before Sentinel’s exposure
scope.population: Active Cybertronian synthetic persons, including deprived miners

societies.description:
Sentinel’s Iacon turns technical power into artificial deprivation. Some Cybertronians have their transformation cogs removed before activation and are forced into mining, while Energon is diverted to the Quintessons. The zero variant therefore has a direct institutional basis: rulers preserve a subordinated labor class rather than sharing the possibilities of their technology. Guarantees are strongly unfavorable for the population that must work under this manufactured hierarchy.

Control is autonomous synthetic authority relative to human ownership, but internally concentrated in Sentinel’s regime. Mechanical bodies do not erase the miners’ useful work or make them nonworking robots. The low participation estimate allows a minority outside ongoing roles while counting mining, transport, repair and administration as labor by persons. It is explicitly a synthetic-person comparison, not a human employment statistic. The missing Matrix also limits current energy supply; the record does not claim that ordinary miners can restore it at will or that every retained task is already unnecessary.

guarantees.basis: Removed capacities, forced work and diverted energy make access insecure.

control.basis: Sentinel holds concentrated synthetic authority independent of organic owners.

nonworking.basis: Active-person scenario retains widespread useful mining, repair and service work.

evidence.claim: Sentinel creates hierarchy by removing transformation cogs and diverts mined Energon.
evidence.locator: Named setting, economy or ending passages; see source read_scope

uncertainties: The exact nonworking share is an editorial scenario for active persons.
The zero variant concerns domination and withheld capacity, not a benevolent job-protection policy.

societies.name: Transformers One — Iacon after the Matrix returns
societies.society: Iacon under the restored Energon flow

scope.period: The realized restoration and explicitly projected early reconstruction
scope.population: Active Cybertronian synthetic residents of Iacon

societies.description:
The ending restores Energon flow and the miners’ transformation cogs, changing both access to a vital material resource and the capacities withheld by the previous regime. That is a realized provision change rather than only a speech promising future abundance. The best-guess floor is strong for Iacon’s active residents, with uncertainty about allocation, infrastructure and the approaching conflict. A restored resource flow is not proof that every desired object is unlimited.

Authority remains autonomous synthetic government relative to biological human ownership. Optimus’s leadership does not establish equal internal control, even as the former class barrier is dismantled. A moderate nonworking estimate allows relief from forced extraction while retaining useful rebuilding, engineering, care-like repair and civic organization. It is a synthetic-person participation proxy, not a claim that machines cannot work. Only the immediate restoration is established; later peaceful guarantees and the percentage doing no useful activity are clearly marked projections rather than a settled postwar constitution.

guarantees.basis: Restored energy and cogs improve implemented access; permanence and equal allocation remain uncertain.

control.basis: Autonomous synthetic leadership persists, with internal sharing not established.

nonworking.basis: Active-person scenario allows extraction relief while retaining reconstruction, repair and civic work.

evidence.claim: The Matrix restores Energon flow and the miners’ transformation cogs.
evidence.locator: Named setting, economy or ending passages; see source read_scope

uncertainties: The durability of the material floor and participation after the ending are projections.
The energy mechanism is treated as a functional technical-production analogue within the film’s synthetic world.
